behavior: Public usize constructors and SetIncrement now reuse the native wrapping roundUpPow2 implementation. Inputs above the highest representable power of two produce internal stride0; zero inputs still produce stride1 and signed constructors retain their clamp policy.
A private constructor accepts already-rounded metadata so Clone and from_moved preserve zero stride rather than applying input normalization again. Copy assignment already copies the stride directly.

Native availableSize computes block count shifted by blockShift, not count multiplied by internalSize. The protected Rust query now uses wrapping shift. With two retained blocks and overflowed stride0, blockShift0 yields availableSize2; ordinary power-of-two strides retain prior results.

64 UBSan-clean native rows compare stride/shift/mask, Size/Length/Lower/Upper, emptiness, retained block count, availableSize, allocator presence and begin/end equality. Inputs include zero, small powers/nonpowers, high-bit boundaries, SIZE_MAX boundaries, all signed extremes and all allocator constructor forms.

Empty unallocated copies/moves retain overflowed metadata, including moved-from source stride and null allocator. Retained empty blocks can be queried, safely reset to their original stride and reused. Nonempty SetIncrement ignores overflow inputs.

Zero-stride element access returns checked index errors; factories and mutable indexing reject before callbacks/allocations; protected typed allocation returns a descriptive domain error. Resetting the empty stride restores normal element behavior. These rejection paths are explicit Rust extensions, not a claim that every native zero-stride mutation is undefined.
All52 original legacy runtime names join to normal and strict Miri results. The complete21 DynamicArray unit filter runs under strict Miri, including the64-row native comparison.
limitations: The new parity domain is constructor/query/clear/reset metadata plus copying/moving empty unallocated arrays. Native element mutations with stride0 are not exercised: some retained layouts may support limited defined access through native shift/mask addressing and require separate per-layout analysis.

Rust checked element/allocation rejection intentionally bounds this metadata domain. Native behavior for failed zero-byte allocation, invalid element lifetimes and out-of-bounds addressing is not reproduced.
The Rust representation stores stride and derives shift/mask; native byte layout, generic allocation ABI and cross-platform widths remain outside this host-specific probe.

Copy constructors and assignment still use Clone convenience policies for payloads; this batch only observes empty transfer metadata. Explicit public copy-construction callback policies remain separate work.
